name: Hubble Space Telescope
headline: length
description: The Hubble Space Telescope is a space telescope launched in 1990 that orbits Earth above the atmosphere. NASA gives it a length of 13.2 m (43.5 ft), a width of 4.2 m (14 ft) at the instrument end, and a weight of about 12,246 kg (27,000 lb), roughly the size and weight of a school bus. Its main mirror is 2.4 m across.

measures.label: Length
measures.note: Overall length of the telescope (43.5 ft)

measures.label: Width
measures.note: Width at the back, where the science instruments are housed (14 ft)

facts.text: NASA says Hubble is approximately the same size and weight as a school bus.
Hubble's 2.4 m (94.5 in) primary mirror is polished so smoothly that, scaled to the diameter of Earth, no bump would stand more than 15 cm (6 in) tall.
Hubble is a Cassegrain reflector powered by two solar arrays.

caveats: Dimensions exclude the two solar arrays, whose size NASA's design page does not give.
